catalog_title: Is the specified generating series involving the number of distinct prime factors of an integer irrational?
original_question_en: Let omega(n) be the number of distinct prime factors of n. Is the series sum_{n>=1} omega(n)/2^n irrational? (Erdos 1948; settled conditionally by K. Pratt, arXiv:2409.15185, under a uniform prime k-tuples conjecture.)
lean_statement_sketch:
def omega (n : Nat) : Nat := (n.primeFactors).card
noncomputable def jsp87Series : Real := tsum fun n => ((omega n : Nat) : Real) * (2:Real)^-(n+1)
theorem jsp_000087_main : jsp87Series.Irrational

-- Round 40 added, in JSPProblem/Periodicity.lean and JSPProblem/LambertTrunc.lean, the full
-- unconditional apparatus of the Erdos--Pratt method on BOTH sides: the exact carry
-- recurrence theta_{N+1} = 2 theta_N - omega N, the uniform bound theta_N >= 1/4, the
-- aperiodicity of omega, the exact clearing denominator of the truncated Lambert sum, and
-- the Lambert-side denominator obstruction.
-- Round 41 added, in JSPProblem/DigitCarry.lean, the exact binary-digit bookkeeping of the carry excess: floor(2^N S) = I N + floor(theta N) (the binary floor is short of the 2-adic prefix by exactly the carry excess), I (N+1) = 2 I N + omega N, the doubling map on fractional parts, the from-scratch theorem that a rational's binary digits are eventually periodic, the identity d N = omega N + c(N+1) - 2 c N, and the endgame theorem 'eventually-periodic carry excess floor(2^N tau N) => jsp87Series is irrational' with its contrapositive.
-- Round 44 added, in JSPProblem/CarryExcess.lean, the QUANTITATIVE SHAPE of the carry excess c N = floor(theta N) and the unconditional sieve content of the correlation hypothesis: omega_ge_two_of_six_dvd and omega_unbounded (omega is unbounded), jsp87Carry_window_lower and jsp87Carry_ge_one_plus_seven (1 + 1/128 <= theta N for every N >= 2, so the carries are NEVER small and the classical 'theta N < 1/b' contradiction is impossible), jsp87CarryExcess_ge_omega and jsp87CarryExcess_unbounded (omega N < 2 c N + 2, hence c N is unbounded, with primorial instances), jsp87Series_irrational_of_carryExcess_bounded (a bounded carry excess would force irrationality, unconditionally, closing the carry-magnitude route in both directions), prod_ge_pow_card / card_largeFactors_le_log / jsp87_sum_omega_window_le (the large prime factors of a window are only logarithmically many) and jsp87_window_rough (for every m, L there is a window of length L with no prime factor in (L, m] -- the small primes of a window are controllable, only the large ones are not), plus the exact bridge jsp87Carry_split (theta N = sum_{k<L} omega (N+k) 2^-(k+1) + 2^-L theta (N+L)) and its corollaries jsp87Carry_le_window and jsp87Carry_le_smallFactors.
-- Round 46 added, in JSPProblem/BlockPeriod.lean, the QUANTITATIVE ARITHMETIC OF THE BASE-2
-- EXPANSION ITSELF -- the new attack family. The t-digit block of the Erdős series, read as a
-- binary integer: def jsp87DigitBlock (N t : Nat) : Int := sum_{j<t} jsp87Digit (N+j) * 2^(t-1-j).
-- jsp87_digitBlock_bounds : 0 <= B N t < 2^t (a block is a genuine t-bit integer);
-- jsp87_digitBlock_step / _shift : periodic digits make the block constant along the period,
--   B (N+q*t) t = B N t. jsp87_floor_telescope : the FINITE TELESCOPING IDENTITY
--   floor (2^(N+t) S) = 2^t * floor (2^N S) + B N t (Mathlib has no statement about the base-2
--   expansion of a real number at all), and jsp87_floor_block_iter : its iteration along the
--   period, (2^t - 1) * floor (2^(N+q*t) S) = 2^(t*q) * K - B N t.
-- THE MAIN THEOREM, jsp87_frac_scaled_eq_block : if the binary digits of S are eventually
--   periodic from N with period t > 0 then Int.fract (2^N * S) = B N t / (2^t - 1). This is
--   the QUANTITATIVE form of 'a rational has eventually periodic binary digits': the
--   denominator of the fractional part is exactly 2^t - 1 (the PERIOD) and the numerator is
--   exactly the digit block. It is the missing half of the Erdos--Pratt method: rounds 38/40
--   only said rationality freezes the carries into (1/b)Z, round 46 says the freeze is explicit.
-- jsp87_period_denominator_obstruction : if S = a/b (b>0) and the digits are eventually
--   periodic with period t, then (2^t - 1) divides b * B N t -- the period-denominator
--   obstruction, pinning the hypothetical rational from above (round 39's
--   dvd_lambert_den_prime_gt pins it from below). jsp87Series_irrational_of_frac_notPeriodic
--   and jsp87Series_rational_imp_frac_periodic : the fractional-part criterion, both directions.
-- jsp87Series_rational_imp_blockConst : the three rigidity conclusions together.

-- Round 51 added, in JSPProblem/PeriodEquation.lean, the PERIOD EQUATION and the
-- omega-WINDOW arithmetic: the t-step form of the carry recurrence with the
-- inhomogeneous term read off, omega N t = sum_{j<t} omega (N+j) 2^(t-1-j) --
-- a weighted average of the omega-values of t consecutive integers, the object a
-- prime-k-tuples correlation hypothesis is supposed to control.  37 new theorems
-- and 4 new definitions, 0 sorry, 0 admit; 488 proved theorems and lemmas in the
-- tree.  New objects: jsp87OmegaWindow, jsp87CarryShift (the lag-t carry
-- increment), jsp87OmegaDiff, jsp87OmegaDiffWindow.  Key results:
-- jsp87Carry_iter (theta (N+t) = 2^t theta N - omega N t, the t-step carry
-- recurrence), jsp87CarryShift_step (THE PERIOD EQUATION, step form, UNCONDITIONAL:
-- omega (N+t) - omega N = 2*Delta N - Delta (N+1), so the whole omega-family is
-- recovered from the carry family), jsp87CarryShift_block (Delta (N+t) = 2^t
-- Delta N - P N t), jsp87CarryShift_eq_excess (under eventual periodicity of the
-- digits the lag-t carry increment equals the lag-t carry-EXCESS increment, an
-- exact integer identity), jsp87_window_periodEquation ((2^t-1) theta N = (c
-- (N+t) - c N) + omega N t), jsp87_carry_block_equation (the same
-- quantisation in block form, (2^t-1) theta N = (2^t-1) c N + B N t),
-- jsp87_window_block_equation (THE HEADLINE: c (N+t) + omega N t = 2^t c N + B
-- N t -- the first exact integer equation in the tree involving a window of
-- omega-values), jsp87_window_block_congr (THE WINDOW CONGRUENCE: 2^t - 1
-- divides c (N+t) - c N + omega N t - B N t, quotient exactly c N -- the first
-- divisibility statement in the carry family and the first time a Mersenne
-- number divides an expression built from omega-values),
-- jsp87_carryExcess_window_le (c (N+t) <= 2^t c N),
-- jsp87_omegaWindow_le_carryExcess (omega N t <= 2^t c N + 2^t - 1),
-- jsp87_omega_diff_periodEquation (THE PERIOD EQUATION on the omega-family: the
-- lag-t omega-difference is exactly the second difference of the carry excess),
-- jsp87_omega_diff_periodEquation_bound (|omega (N+t) - omega N| <= 6 log_2 (N+t+1)
-- under eventual periodicity), jsp87_dyadic_iff_carryInt (S = n/2^M iff the
-- carry theta M is an integer), jsp87_carryInt_iff_digitZero (hence the binary
-- digits of S are eventually 0 iff some carry is an integer -- the period-1
-- sub-case in carry language), jsp87_carry_int_ge_two (under the dyadic
-- hypothesis c N >= 2, unconditionally c N >= 1), jsp87_dyadic_omega_eq (under
-- the dyadic hypothesis omega N = 2 c N - c (N+1): the whole omega-family is a
-- doubling-difference of the carry excess), jsp87_dyadic_omega_bounds (the
-- squeeze 2 c N - log_2(N+1) <= omega N <= 2 c N - 2),
-- jsp87Series_irrational_of_omegaWindow_never_congr (THE FIFTH IRRATIONALITY
-- CRITERION: if no candidate period passes the window congruence test, S is
-- irrational).  The development now has five independent aperiodicity criteria,
-- on the carry excess, the binary digit string, the primary digit string, the
-- doubling orbit of the carries, and the omega-window modulo 2^t - 1.
-- Round 52 added, in JSPProblem/AdicPrefix.lean, the 2-ADIC AND MODULAR ARITHMETIC
-- of the BINARY PREFIX I N = floor (2^N S) - floor (theta N) -- the numerator of the
-- N-th partial sum, the integer whose binary expansion is the first N digits of S and
-- the 2-adic integer whose digits are the omega-values with carries.  NO earlier round
-- had ever looked at this object: rounds 37-46 attacked the carried series, 47 the
-- carry-free expansion, 48 the doubling map, 49 the radix, 50 the asymptotics, 51 the
-- period equation.  The driving observation is the homogeneous form of the prefix
-- recursion: jsp87Prefix_iter : I (N+t) = 2^t I N + Omega N t, whose inhomogeneous term
-- is EXACTLY round 51's omega-window, whence jsp87Prefix_dvd_window : 2^t | I (N+t)
-- <-> 2^t | Omega N t (THE 2-ADIC WINDOW EQUIVALENCE).  Headline:
-- jsp87_prefix_mod_not_eventuallyPeriodic -- the binary prefix is APERIODIC MODULO
-- EVERY m >= 2, a sixth independent aperiodicity statement in the tree and the first
-- on this object, proved from round 49's aperiodicity of omega modulo every m >= 2 by
-- the transfer lemma jsp87Prefix_periodic_imp_omega_periodic (which uses the recursion
-- I (N+1) = 2 I N + omega N and Nat.ModEq.add_left_cancel).  Also new: the 2-adic
-- exponent jsp87Val2 with its exact specification and the sawtooth
-- jsp87Val2_prefix_succ_even (v (I (N+1)) = v (I N + omega N / 2) + 1); the parity and
-- chain theorems jsp87Prefix_parity / jsp87Prefix_dvd_two_iff /
-- jsp87Prefix_dvd_pow_succ; the escape statement
-- jsp87_prefix_dvd_pow_two_not_eventually (the prefix escapes every fixed power of 2
-- infinitely often); the transfer jsp87_window_periodic_of_prefix_periodic (modular
-- periodicity of the prefix forces the same of the omega-window); and
-- jsp87_adic_carry_congr, the first statement reading the 2-adic content of the binary
-- prefix off the carry excess: under eventual periodicity of the digits with period t,
-- 2^t | I (N+t) <-> 2^t | (c (N+t) - B N t).
-- Round 55 added, in JSPProblem/SieveModel.lean, the full SIEVE LOCAL MODEL: the primorial, the exact window-wise periodicity of the small-factor content of omega (jsp87SmallFactors_congr, sieveProfile_period), the realisation of every sieve profile at arbitrary height (jsp87SieveProfile_recurs), the power form of the unsieved-content bound ((k+1)^r <= m), the compensation form of round 53's constant-run hypothesis (jsp87_constRun_sieve_iff / jsp87_constRun_sieve_sub), the criterion jsp87Series_irrational_of_sieveRun, the machine-checked negative jsp87_run_halves_not_constant and the height bound jsp87_constRun_height (3^(u-1) <= N+L-1).  40 new theorems, zero sorry.

notes: ROUND 64 -- NEW ATTACK FAMILY: THE DOUBLING ORBIT COMPUTED EXACTLY, AND THE DEATH OF THE 2-ADIC LIMIT.  lean/JSPProblem/OrbitArith.lean (999 lines, 1 new definition, 40 new theorems and lemmas, 0 sorry, 0 admit, 0 new linter warnings).  The tree is zero-sorry with 822 proved theorems and lemmas (was 781).  (1) NEW OBJECT jsp87OrbitNum r a b N = (2^N a) mod b, the numerator of the doubling orbit of the carries, with jsp87OrbitNum_succ: r (N+1) = 2 r (N) mod b (the numerators ARE the orbit of the doubling map on Z/bZ, hence deterministic).  (2) jsp87_fracCarry_eq_orbitNum: THE ORBIT POINT IS A RESIDUE -- for S = a/b with 0 < a and 1 <= N, Int.fract (theta N) = (2^N a mod b)/b, via the from-scratch lemma Int.fract_natCast_div_nat_cast (fract (p/q) = (p mod q)/q).  (3) FLAGSHIP jsp87_fracCarryPeriod_iff_oddPart_dvd_mer: THE COMPLETE PERIOD-ORDER CORRESPONDENCE FOR THE ORBIT -- for S = a/b in lowest terms, 1 <= M with v_2(b) <= M and 0 < t, (forall N >= M, fract (theta (N+t)) = fract (theta N)) <-> jsp87OddPart b | 2^t - 1; the minimal eventual period of the orbit IS the multiplicative order of 2 modulo the odd part of the denominator, and the orbit is never periodic before the 2-adic threshold.  (4) jsp87_fracCarry_period_sub_iff (two periods spawn a smaller one), jsp87_fracCarry_period_dvd (the periods are gcd-closed, via round 39's gcd_two_pow_sub_one), jsp87_fracCarry_distinct and jsp87_fracCarry_distinct_card (a minimal period visits exactly t pairwise distinct points).  (5) jsp87_fracCarry_periodic_imp_digitPeriodic and jsp87_fracCarry_period_iff_digitPeriod: THE ORBIT AND THE BINARY DIGIT STRING HAVE EXACTLY THE SAME EVENTUAL PERIODS, from the same start point; hence jsp87Series_irrational_iff_fracCarry_notPeriodic, the COMPLETE (iff) Erdos criterion on the carry orbit (round 48 proved only one direction).  (6) the dyadic dichotomy: jsp87_fracCarry_zero_of_dyadic, jsp87_dyadic_iff_orbit_period_one (period 1 = dyadic), jsp87_fracCarry_zero_iff_dyadic, jsp87_fracCarry_pos_of_oddPart and jsp87_dyadic_or_fracCarry_pos (the orbit hits 0 only for a dyadic value; otherwise 0 < fract (theta N) for EVERY N >= 1).  (7) NEGATIVE, MACHINE-CHECKED, IMPORTANT: jsp87_prefix_twoAdic_limit_absent -- THE 2-ADIC VALUE OF THE ERDOs SERIES DOES NOT EXIST (no k >= 1 and no M make the binary prefix coherent mod 2^k on a tail), because coherence forces omega to be constant mod 2^k (jsp87_prefix_coh_omega_congr) while omega p = 1 at a prime and omega (2p) = 2 (jsp87_omega_one_of_prime, jsp87_omega_two_mul_of_prime); with jsp87_prefix_escapes_every_pow_two and jsp87_prefix_incoherent_at_prime.  (8) ROUND 52'S NAMED BLOCKER jsp87_prefix_window_congr_fails IS CLOSED: jsp87_omegaWindow_not_dvd_pow_two (via jsp87_omegaWindow_parity and jsp87_omegaWindow_not_even_of_prime) proves that for every t >= 1 and every M there is N >= M with 2^t NOT dividing the omega-window, witnessed at a prime.  (9) instances: ord_7(2) = 3, ord_3(2) = 2 with v_2(12) = 2 (the 2-adic threshold of 12 is exact), ord_9(2) = 6, and the distinctness of the three residue orbit points of a 7-period.

round46_blocker.name: jsp87Series_irrational_of_blockNotPeriodic
round46_blocker.statement: for every t > 0 the sequence N |-> jsp87DigitBlock N t = sum_{j<t} jsp87Digit (N+j) * 2^(t-1-j) is NOT eventually periodic in N
round46_blocker.why_it_is_the_exact_remainder: Rounds 40+41 gave (rationality => digits eventually periodic => omega eventually periodic => contradiction with omega_not_eventuallyPeriodic). Round 46 makes the implication quantitative: eventual periodicity of the digits makes the t-digit block constant along the period (jsp87_digitBlock_shift) and makes the fractional part exactly B N t / (2^t - 1) (jsp87_frac_scaled_eq_block), while jsp87_frac_scaled_block_const shows the fractional part is then constant. So aperiodicity of the block is NECESSARY for irrationality, and the reduction is complete in both directions except for this one statement. Supplying it requires a uniform prime-k-tuples correlation hypothesis on omega at shifted primes -- Pratt's hypothesis (arXiv:2409.15185), an assumption of the published result and not of the catalog statement, hence not introduced here.
round46_blocker.not_a_mathlib_gap: there is no Mathlib lemma on the base-2 expansion of a real, on the digits of a Lambert-type series, or on correlations of omega; the entire apparatus is from scratch

round49_blocker.statement: jsp87_fracCarry_not_eventuallyPeriodic -- the doubling orbit N |-> Int.fract (theta N), i.e. the fractional part of the carry of the Erdős series, is not eventually periodic in N (equivalently, via jsp87_digit_eq_fractCarry, the binary digit string of jsp87Series is not eventually periodic).
round49_blocker.why_not_proved: The round-49 radix family proves the criterion in every radix and exhibits THREE new complete irrationality theorems, but jsp87_noCarry_fails_any_radix shows the criterion is inapplicable to jsp87Series in every radix (omega is unbounded, so the Erdős series carries). Nothing unconditional is known about the fluctuations of the carry; supplying this is the arithmetic content of the uniform prime k-tuples hypothesis in Pratt (arXiv:2409.15185), an assumption of the PUBLISHED result and not of the catalog statement.
round49_blocker.gate: jsp_000087_main remains deliberately undeclared: the headline irrationality is conditional in the literature and the catalog records 'Solved; Lean proof: No; Eligible to claim: No'.

round50_blocker.name: jsp87_digitDensity_not_bounded
round50_blocker.statement: the number of 1-digits among the first N binary digits of the Erdős series, D N = sum_{M<N} jsp87Digit M, is bounded by NO linear function of N along an unbounded sequence; formally (forall C > 0) (forall K) (exists N >= K) D N > C * N
round50_blocker.why_it_is_the_exact_remainder: Round 50 proved jsp87Series_rational_imp_digitCount_linear and jsp87_digitCount_periodic_bounds: if S = a/b with b > 0 then the binary digits of S are eventually periodic, whence D N lies in [D M, D M + N + t] for all N >= M, i.e. the digit count grows exactly linearly. jsp87Series_irrational_of_digitDensity_not_bounded is the contrapositive. Equivalently, via jsp87_digitCount_eq_fractSum (D N + fract (2^N S) = S + sum_{M<N} fract (2^M S)) and round 41's jsp87_digit_eq_fract, the MEAN of the doubling orbit N |-> fract (2^N S) must fail to be bounded by any linear function.
round50_blocker.not_a_mathlib_gap: Mathlib contains no statement whatsoever about the base-2 expansion of a real number (no digit function, no floor-digit identity, no doubling orbit), hence no statement about the rate of accumulation of 1-digits; the whole development is from scratch
round50_blocker.attack_family_this_round: ASYMPTOTIC CARRY THEORY -- new family. Rounds 37-46 attacked the carried series through periodicity (Lambert reduction, carry scaffold, gcd arithmetic, carry dynamics, digit bookkeeping, carry-excess/sieve content, base-2 block arithmetic), round 47 the carry-free (primary) expansion, round 48 the doubling map on the carries, round 49 the criterion in arbitrary radix. This round changes the QUESTION rather than the tool: how FAST can the carry excess grow, and how FAST does the binary digit string accumulate 1s. The single observation is that the carry is a geometrically weighted average of the omega-values after the cut point, so omega m <= log_2 m makes the carry SUBLINAR. Concretely: theta N = sum'_k omega (N+k) 2^{-(k+1)} (jsp87Carry_eq_tsum) and theta N <= log_2 N + log_2 e / N (jsp87Carry_le_logb_sharp) -- the FIRST sublinear upper bound on the carry (rounds 38-40 had only the linear theta N <= N+1). Combined with round 44's c N >= 1 and unboundedness this yields the LOGARITHMIC WINDOW jsp87CarryExcess_window: 1 <= c N <= k+3 for 2 <= N <= 2^{k+1}, and jsp87CarryExcess_unbounded_beyond: the carry excess escapes every such range.

round51_blocker.statement: for every candidate period t > 0 and every start point M there is a cut point N >= M at which 2^t - 1 does NOT divide c (N+t) - c N + Omega N t - B N t, where Omega N t = sum_{j<t} omega (N+j) 2^(t-1-j) is the omega-window and B N t = jsp87DigitBlock N t the t-digit block; i.e. the residue of the omega-window modulo the Mersenne number 2^t - 1 does not match the digit block

round53_blocker.statement: the constant-run hypothesis: for every L >= 1 there are a place N >= 1 and a value u with omega constant on [N, N+L) and (u-1) <= theta (N+L) < u, i.e. blocks of arbitrarily long consecutive integers all having the same number of distinct prime factors, positioned so that the carry does not overshoot.  This is a uniform prime-tuples-type statement about PATTERNS of omega on consecutive integers (the same shape as the hypothesis of Pratt arXiv:2409.15185), it is NOT known, and it is the single input still missing for jsp_000087_main.
round53_blocker.proved_conditional_on_it: jsp87Series_irrational_of_constRun -- fully proved, no sorry: the constant-run hypothesis implies jsp87Series.Irrational, via jsp87Series_irrational_of_digit_run_ones and jsp87Series_irrational_of_fract_near_one.
round53_blocker.unconditional_instances: jsp87_digit_run_twenty (three consecutive 1s at 20,21,22), jsp87Series_rational_imp_denominator_ge_eight (S = a/b with b > 0 forces b >= 8), jsp87Series_rational_imp_denominator_ge (a run of L ones forces 2^L <= b).
round53_blocker.not_a_criterion: runs of 0s: jsp87_fractCarry_small_or_zero proves a tiny orbit value is either exactly 0 or forces b > 2^L, and 0 cannot be excluded (dyadic rationals have an eventually-zero digit string), so the dual of jsp87Series_irrational_of_digit_run_ones is FALSE.

round55_blocker.name: jsp87Series_irrational_of_sieveRun
round55_blocker.statement: for every L >= 1 there are N >= 1, a cut-off k >= 1 and u >= 1 with jsp87SieveCard (N+j) k + jsp87UnsievedCard (N+j) k = u for every j < L and (u-1) <= jsp87Carry (N+L) < u; then jsp87Series is irrational
round55_blocker.why_it_is_the_exact_remainder: The analytic half of the Erdos-Pratt argument is complete in Lean (rounds 51-53): a constant run of omega produces a run of L ones in the binary expansion of S, and runs of ones of unbounded length force irrationality.  Round 55 shows the residual hypothesis is entirely about the primes exceeding a fixed bound k: the small-prime half is periodic modulo k# (jsp87SmallFactors_congr) and realisable at every height (jsp87SieveProfile_recurs), and the unsieved half is logarithmically bounded (jsp87Unsieved_le_log).
round55_blocker.not_a_mathlib_gap: no Mathlib statement about prime-k-tuples, about the number of prime factors of consecutive integers, or about any sieve; the local model was built from scratch this round

jsp87SieveProfile_recurs: every sieve profile of level k occurs at every height N0
jsp87_pow_unsieved_le: (k+1)^r <= m for r = # prime divisors of m exceeding k

jsp87_constRun_sieve_iff / jsp87_constRun_sieve_sub: the compensation form of the constant-run hypothesis
jsp87_run_halves_not_constant: NEGATIVE, machine-checked -- the two halves of a constant run are not separately constant
jsp87_constRun_height: a constant run of value u on [N,N+L), L >= 2, forces 3^(u-1) <= N+L-1

negative_knowledge: The round-53 plan of weakening the hypothesis by requiring the two halves to be constant separately is REFUTED in this form (jsp87_run_halves_not_constant).
The sieve content is not periodic at n = 0 (every prime divides 0, but 0 has no prime factors); all periodicity statements carry 1 <= n.

round64_blocker.name: jsp87Series_irrational_of_blockNotPeriodic (equivalently: aperiodicity of the doubling orbit of the carries)
round64_blocker.statement: for every t > 0 the sequence N |-> jsp87DigitBlock N t = sum_{j<t} jsp87Digit (N+j) 2^(t-1-j) is NOT eventually periodic in N
round64_blocker.why_it_is_the_exact_remainder: By round 64 the reduction is an EQUIVALENCE in both directions: jsp87Series_irrational_iff_fracCarry_notPeriodic identifies irrationality with the aperiodicity of Int.fract (theta N), and jsp87_fracCarryPeriod_iff_oddPart_dvd_mer computes that aperiodicity arithmetically -- the orbit's minimal eventual period is ord_{jsp87OddPart b}(2) and it starts at v_2(b), the same integer that governs the digit string.  The 2-adic alternative is closed by a theorem (jsp87_prefix_twoAdic_limit_absent).  So the single remaining step is aperiodicity of the real doubling orbit, equivalently of the binary digit string, which is the arithmetic content of the uniform prime-k-tuples hypothesis of Pratt's result (arXiv:2409.15185) -- an assumption of the PUBLISHED result, not of the catalog statement.
round64_blocker.not_a_mathlib_gap: Mathlib contains no statement whatsoever about the base-2 expansion of a real number (no digit function, no floor-digit identity, no doubling orbit, no residue description of a fractional part); the entire development is from scratch
